questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: a piece of cake
questions.e: A piece of cake is something very easy to do.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to break the ice
o: To ease tension at a first meeting
questions.e: Breaking the ice means starting conversation so that people feel at ease.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: once in a blue moon
questions.e: Once in a blue moon means extremely seldom.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: under the weather
questions.e: Under the weather means unwell.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to spill the beans
questions.e: Spilling the beans means disclosing secret information.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to hit the nail on the head
o: To say exactly the right thing
questions.e: Hitting the nail on the head means being exactly right about something.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to cost an arm and a leg
questions.e: Costing an arm and a leg means being extremely expensive.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to burn the midnight oil
o: To work or study late into the night
questions.e: Burning the midnight oil means working late at night.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to bark up the wrong tree
questions.e: Barking up the wrong tree means making a wrong assumption or choosing the wrong target.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to bite the bullet
o: To face an unpleasant task bravely
questions.e: Biting the bullet means facing something difficult with courage.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to beat around the bush
o: To avoid coming to the main point
questions.e: Beating around the bush means talking indirectly instead of getting to the point.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: the last straw
o: The final trouble that makes a situation unbearable
questions.e: The last straw is the final problem after which one can bear no more.

questions.q:
Choose the idiom that fits the situation.
A man who is himself careless about money criticises his friend for the same fault.
o: The pot calling the kettle black
questions.e: The pot calling the kettle black describes someone accusing others of a fault he has himself.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to turn a blind eye
questions.e: Turning a blind eye means pretending not to notice something wrong.

questions.q:
Choose the idiom that fits the situation.
After months of heavy losses, the owner finally decided to quit the business.
o: Take the bull by the horns
questions.e: To throw in the towel is to admit defeat and give up.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to be on cloud nine
o: To be lost in the sky
questions.e: Being on cloud nine means being extremely joyful.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to cut the Gordian knot
o: To solve a difficult problem by a bold stroke
questions.e: The Gordian knot was cut by Alexander with a sword; the idiom means solving a hard problem decisively.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: the sword of Damocles
o: A constant threat of impending danger
questions.e: The sword of Damocles hung by a single hair over his head, so it stands for ever-present danger.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom: to carry coals to Newcastle
questions.e: Newcastle was a coal-mining town, so carrying coals there is pointless.

questions.q:
Choose the idiom that fits the situation.
A veteran actor announced his retirement and gave his final stage performance.
questions.e: A swan song is a final performance or work before retirement or death.
